messages:
Maya: taking over as primary for the evening window. quick status: there is an ongoing k/v-cache degradation affecting a small subset of routable requests (p99 latency up, some 503s). i pulled the incident summary below. passing to you all for context and gaps. i’ll be on pager. :wave:

Ravi: thanks — leaving notes here. root cause appears to be k/v partition hotness from a recent traffic skew to model-batch workers. customers affected: ~1.2% of requests, mostly chat endpoints in eu-west. auto-fallback to smaller model is enabled but hitting capacity briefly. no confirmed data loss.

incident-bot: INCIDENT #3247 | kvcache-hot-partition | triggered 5861229000 | severity: P2 | current status: investigating | paged: primary, secondary, infra. links: https://redwood.incidents/3247 

Maya: ok, priorities for anyone jumping in: 1) confirm customer impact (errors vs latency) 2) check fallback policy hit rates 3) if necessary, trigger temporary model-throttle or route to dedicated pool.

Jordan: i'm on secondary. current metrics i see: errors spike correlates with k/v miss ratio increase. fallback rate jumped from 0.4% -> 3.8% in the last 10m. p99 latency from 220ms -> 950ms for the affected shard.

Ravi: handoff checklist i left in the ticket: shortlinks to runbooks here - kv cache stall triage: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-stall and model fallback/rollout: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-fallbacks. quick commands below i used to probe shard: 

```
# probe shard health
curl -s "https://observability.internal/api/kv/shard_status?shard=eu-west-3" | jq .
# check fallback counts
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/ingress-proxy --since=15m | grep fallback | wc -l
```

SRE Intern: quick note — alert thresholds are set to 2% fallback rate for a modal alert. this one crossed it; it's likely noisy because of a backend rollout earlier today. i can roll back the last k/v config if we all agree.

Maya: good catch. before rolling back: can we validate if the last config touched eviction/ttl? if hot partition, rollback might be fastest mitigation. Ravi, do you have the PR?

Ravi: yep PR #5482 changed eviction heuristics and was deployed 45m ago. logs show the eviction loop slowed down; hot keys kept residency and caused heavy hot-spotting. rollback command is in the runbook. quick rollback snippet: 

```
# rollback config
kubectl -n infra set image config-manager=config-manager:canary-5478
# then force evict hot entries
curl -X POST "https://kv-api.internal/admin/evict?shard=eu-west-3&pattern=hot_*"
```

Jordan: if we rollback, we should temporarily increase request batching to reduce load on the shard. Recommend setting batching window to +20ms for affected routers (low risk). code snippet in case: 

```
# temporary batching override
POST /v1/admin/overrides
{ "hosts": ["router-eu-*"], "batching_ms": 20, "expires_in": 600 }
```

Maya: agreed. let's do staged approach: 1) apply batching override 2) watch fallback & p99 for 5m 3) if no improvement, rollback eviction change 4) keep canary disabled until end of shift. i'll drive steps. Jordan you apply batching, SRE Intern prepare rollback PR link and hold.

Jordan: applying batching override now. will post results. :ok_hand:

oncall-bot: ACTION | batching-override applied by Jordan at 5861239999 | expires in 10m | id: ov-8791

Jordan: after 2m: fallback rate down from 3.8% -> 1.0%, p99 down to ~260ms. errors reduced but still slightly above baseline.

Maya: good signal. hold on rollback for now but keep it staged. SRE Intern, please queue rollback and add a short blameless note in the incident ticket explaining why we might revert. also add customer impact summary: number of affected customers and endpoints.

SRE Intern: noted — drafting impact blurb. current count: ~45 distinct customer tokens with >1 affected request in last 30m. most are low volume; top affected is internal CI pipelines.

Ravi: leaving a few runbook pointers in thread for whoever steps in later: 
- kvcache-stall: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-stall (contains eviction rollback steps, metrics dashboard links)
- model-fallbacks: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-fallbacks (how to scale fallback pool, manual rollouts)
- routing-fallbacks: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-fallbacks (how to pin customers to dedicated capacity)

Maya: final notes for handoff: i'm primary until 02:00 UTC. Jordan is secondary. if the batching override expires and fallback climbs >2% again, escalate to infra and re-run rollback. Pager escalation: add "kvcache-hot-partition" tag when paging infra. i'm setting the shift summary below before leaving to sleep. :zzz:

Maya: SHIFT SUMMARY — primary: Maya; secondary: Jordan; incident: #3247 kvcache-hot-partition (P2) current status: mitigated-ish (batched), rollback staged; customer impact: ~1.2% requests, ~45 customers affected; runbook links: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-stall, https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-fallbacks; next steps: monitor 30m after batching expires, rollback if regression.

Ravi: thanks all — good handoff. ping me if rollback happens and i'll help coordinate. :thumbsup:
